title: Article 291 — Privy purse sums of Rulers (Omitted)

content.overview: Article 291 guaranteed payment of privy purse sums to Rulers of former Indian States, charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and tax-exempt. It was omitted by the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971, section 2, with effect from 28 December 1971. The same amendment abolished privy purses, inserted Article 363A (cessation of recognition of Rulers), and relatedly omitted Article 362.
content.glance: Art 291 omitted by 26th Amendment 1971 (w.e.f. 28-12-1971). Privy purses abolished; see Article 363A.
content.study:
Article 291 constitutionalised covenant-based privy purse payments to recognised Rulers.

Omission: Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971, s. 2 (w.e.f. 28-12-1971). Privy purses were abolished; recognition of Rulers for that purpose ceased under the newly inserted Article 363A; Article 362 (privileges of Rulers) was also omitted.

Examination rule: Do not cite Article 291 as living law. Historical questions should state the 26th Amendment abolition of privy purses.

sections.heading: Constitutional status
sections.body: Omitted by the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971, s. 2 (w.e.f. 28-12-1971). Companion changes: omission of Article 362; insertion of Article 363A; amendment of the definition of ‘Ruler’ in Article 366.

sections.heading: Exam checkpoints
sections.body:
1. State 26th Amendment and 28-12-1971 effective date.
2. Link Art 291 (purses), Art 362 (privileges), and Art 363A (cessation of recognition).
3. Do not treat privy purse claims as constitutionally enforceable under omitted Article 291.

examples.title: Illustration — Post-1971 claim
examples.body: A claim in 2026 for payment of privy purse under Article 291 fails at the threshold: the article was omitted and privy purses abolished by the 26th Amendment.

misconceptions.trap: Privy purses remain a constitutional entitlement under Article 291.
misconceptions.correction: Article 291 was omitted by the 26th Amendment, 1971. Privy purses were abolished.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the status of Article 291?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 291 was omitted by the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971 (w.e.f. 28-12-1971). Privy purses were abolished. Recognition consequences are addressed in Article 363A.

examTips: Always pair Arts 291 and 362 omissions with Art 363A insertion under the 26th Amendment.
content.migrationNote: Remediated 2026-10-09: accurate 26th Amendment omission and privy-purse abolition. Case-law gate open.

notes: Omission by 26th Amendment w.e.f. 28-12-1971 recorded from standard official sources. No case holdings invented.
